mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real GDP growth above 3% annualized for two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 3% annualized for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 exceeds 3% annualized for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (CPIAUCSL) where PAYEMS grows faster than CPIAUCSL by more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals increased household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > CPIAUCSL growth by >0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and reduced economic output, which correlates with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the housing starts index (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals restrictive monetary policy coinciding with a housing contraction, which reduces investment and consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND HOUST falls >10% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS rises and HOUST falls by more than 10% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.
